description: pytest + SQLAlchemy rule patterns (#6927, python arm). Four `^`-anchored patterns in pytest.yaml and sqlalchemy.yaml were compiled without `(?m)`, so `^` meant start-of-TEXT and each could only fire on a file's opening construct. Every file here opens with a docstring, so the pre-fix binary extracted ZERO Test, TestClass, Schema and Model entities from those four rules. The fixture varies ONE axis — the vertical position of each construct (never line 1; one indented inside a class; one last-in-file) — and holds the constructs at their idiomatic spellings. It grades BOTH directions: src/tests/helpers.py and src/app/serializers.py declare nothing and exist only to supply forbidden rows, because a recall assertion cannot see a pattern that started matching too much (#6902).

expected_entities.name: test_creates_customer
expected_entities.note: #6927 recall arm. Module-level test AFTER a docstring, an import block and a fixture. Extracted ZERO before the fix.

expected_entities.name: test_rejects_negative_amount
expected_entities.note: The LAST construct in the file — furthest possible position from start-of-text.

expected_entities.name: TestInvoiceTotals
expected_entities.note: #6927 recall arm for `^class\s+(Test\w+)`. The capture accepts any `Test*` name, which is pytest's OWN python_classes default rather than an over-fire, so it was left as written.

expected_entities.name: customer
expected_entities.note: CONTROL, held constant. The @pytest.fixture pattern is NOT `^`-anchored, so it was green before the fix and must stay green. Without it, 'the rules came back' and 'rule loading broke entirely' would look the same.

expected_entities.name: Registry
expected_entities.note: #6927 recall arm for `(?m)^class\s+(\w+)\s*\([^)]*DeclarativeBase[^)]*\)`, and the ONLY row that grades it. In app/models.py the two class patterns both match `class Base(DeclarativeBase):` and the downstream class-shadow fold collapses the result, so removing `(?m)` from the DeclarativeBase pattern there changed NOTHING observable — measured, not assumed: the mutant left the fixture at an identical 57 entities and an identical recall. app/db.py declares `class Registry(MappedAsDataclass, DeclarativeBase):`, whose two-name base list the Model pattern's `\(\w+\)` cannot match, so this Schema entity has exactly one producer. No source_file: the graph carries no file attribution for it.

expected_entities.name: Base
expected_entities.note: FINDING, pinned rather than papered over: `class Base(DeclarativeBase):` satisfies BOTH class patterns — the Model one because `(\w+)` accepts `DeclarativeBase` as a single simple base — so the declarative base is minted twice. Unreachable while the anchor defect kept both patterns dead; `(?m)` makes it live. Recorded so a later narrowing is a deliberate change rather than an accident.

expected_entities.name: Customer
expected_entities.note: #6927 recall arm for `^class\s+([A-Z]\w*)\s*\(\w+\)`, which also carries `requires_framework: true` — see the forbidden rows for why.

expected_entities.name: Invoice
expected_entities.note: CONTROL, held constant: `= relationship("Invoice")` is un-anchored, green before and after.

expected_entities.name: customers.id
expected_entities.note: CONTROL, held constant: `ForeignKey("customers.id")` is un-anchored, green before and after.

forbidden_entities.name: test_commented_out
forbidden_entities.note: #6927 forbidden arm, ANCHOR direction. src/tests/helpers.py holds `# def test_commented_out(client):`. A `#` opens the line, so ONLY the line anchor keeps it out — dropping the `^` from `(?m)^def\s+(test_\w+)` mints it. Verified capable of firing by that mutant, not assumed (#6938).

forbidden_entities.name: TestCommentedOut
forbidden_entities.note: Same, for `(?m)^class\s+(Test\w+)`: `# class TestCommentedOut:` in src/tests/helpers.py.

forbidden_entities.name: test_nested_helper
forbidden_entities.note: `def test_nested_helper(inner):` indented inside `build_client()` in src/tests/helpers.py. Kept out by the anchor alone; widening it to `^\s*def` mints it. This row is what makes that widening a deliberate change with a forbidden row to move, rather than a silent one.

forbidden_entities.name: TestNestedHelper
forbidden_entities.note: #6927 forbidden arm, INDENTED direction for the CLASS anchor. PR #6943 review R3: the `def` anchor was pinned on two axes (a `#`-commented line and an indented one) and the `class` anchor on only one, so `(?m)^class\s+(Test\w+)` -> `(?m)^\s*class\s+(Test\w+)` left the engine suite green AND this fixture at exit 0, 10/10, zero forbidden hits — its column-0 half was graded by nothing, and a nested `class TestX:` is production-reachable. `class TestNestedHelper:` is declared inside `build_client()` in src/tests/helpers.py; that widening is what mints it.

forbidden_entities.name: LegacyInvoice
forbidden_entities.note: #6927 forbidden arm, ANCHOR direction for the Model rule — and deliberately inside src/app/models.py, which DOES import sqlalchemy. The serializers.py rows below are kept out by the framework GATE and so say nothing about the anchor; this row satisfies the gate and is kept out by the anchor alone, so the two fences are graded separately and their mutants are distinguishable.

forbidden_entities.name: ConfigError
forbidden_entities.note: #6927 forbidden arm, BLAST-RADIUS direction, and the reason this change is not `(?m)` alone. `^class\s+([A-Z]\w*)\s*\(\w+\)\s*:` describes a module-level class with one simple base — plain Python syntax — and Detect resolves rule sets by file.Language, so under `(?m)` it would type EVERY such class in EVERY indexed Python file as a Model. src/app/serializers.py names sqlalchemy nowhere; `requires_framework: true` (the #6152 remedy already applied to falcon/cherrypy) is what holds it. Removing that key mints this entity.

forbidden_entities.name: Serializer
forbidden_entities.note: Second row for the same fence, on `class Serializer(object):` — one row could be held by an accident of the name, two of different shapes cannot.

forbidden_entities.name: ConfigError
forbidden_entities.note: Sweep of the OTHER kind sqlalchemy.yaml's class patterns can mint, so a mutant that widened the DeclarativeBase pattern instead of the Model one is also caught.

forbidden_entities.name: SessionFactory
forbidden_entities.note: #6927 forbidden arm, CAPTURE direction. PR #6943 review R2: widening the Model pattern's `\(\w+\)` to `\([^)]*\)` was distinguishable and ungraded. On `Registry` it is invisible — that class already carries a Schema entity, so the second mint is absorbed by the class-shadow fold and surfaces only as an accidental recall loss with ZERO forbidden hits. `class SessionFactory(LoggingMixin, BaseFactory):` in src/app/db.py has a two-name base list, no DeclarativeBase and no second producer, so the same widening lands here as a visible false Model.

expected_relationships.note: #6927 recall arm at the EDGE level. BOTH endpoints are entities the widened Model pattern mints, so this edge does not exist at all unless the anchor fix holds — it is the downstream consequence of the fix, not a restatement of it. It also keeps this fixture from being exempted by `asserts_no_relationships`, which would leave edge extraction for this language graded by nothing.
Same edge for the model declared LAST in the file.
